929.t: From Proto-Hellenic *odónts, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃dónts (“tooth”). Cognates include Sanskrit दत् (dát), Latin dēns and Old English tōþ (English tooth).

911.t: From Proto-Hellenic *plḗtʰō, from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₁- with root extension like plebs. Cognates include Latin pleo, Sanskrit पिपर्ति (piparti, “to fill”) and Avestan 𐬵𐬀𐬨𐬞𐬁𐬟𐬭𐬁𐬌𐬙𐬌 (hampāfrāⁱti).

979.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *stegʷʰ- Proto-Indo-European *-eti Proto-Indo-European *stégʷʰeti Proto-Hellenic *stékʷʰō Ancient Greek στέφω (stéphō) Proto-Indo-European *-nós Ancient Greek -νος (-nos) Ancient Greek στέφανος From στέφω (stéphō, “to…

975.t: Adverbial use of the stem of ἐΰς (eǘs, “good”), from Proto-Hellenic *ehu-, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁su- (“good”).

961.t: From Proto-Hellenic *génetis, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵénh₁tis. Synchronically, a verbal noun from γίγνομαι (gígnomai, “to come into being”) + -σις (-sĭs).

926.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *ster- Proto-Indo-European *sterh₃- Proto-Indo-European *-tós Proto-Indo-European *str̥tós Proto-Hellenic *strətós Ancient Greek στρατός (stratós) Proto-Indo-European *h₂eǵ- Proto-Indo-European *-eti Proto-Indo-European…

918.t: Of uncertain origin. Often explained as a derivative in *-iyo- from a participal form *s-o-to-s, beside alleged Proto-Indo-European *seto-s in ἐτάζω (etázō, “to examine, test”), although this account presents difficulties.

992.t: The present stem is from Proto-Hellenic *gʷəňňō, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷm̥yéti, from zero-grade of *gʷem- + *-yéti. Cognates include Old English cuman (English come), Latin veniō, and Sanskrit गन्ति॑ (gánti).

928.t: From ἐξοντ- (exont-, participle) + -ία (-ĭ́ā, verbal adjective suffix), from ἔξεστι (éxesti, “it is possible, it is allowed”).

996.t: Borrowed from Biblical Hebrew רָחֵל (rāḥēl), from Proto-Semitic *raḫil-.

986.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂er- (“thus, so”), probably as a grammaticalization of the sense "to fit, fix". Cognates include Lithuanian ir̃ (“and; so”).

924.t: From Proto-Indo-European *pleh₁- (“to fill”). Cognates include Latin pleō, Sanskrit पिप॑र्ति (píparti, “to fill”) and Avestan 𐬵𐬀𐬨𐬞𐬁𐬟𐬭𐬁𐬌𐬙𐬌 (hampāfrāⁱti).

977.t: According to Beekes, from a Pre-Greek root common to κόρυμβος (kórumbos, “tip of a ship or mountain”) and κόρυς (kórus, “helmet”), based on κορυφ-/κορυμβ- alternation with the aforementioned κόρυμβος (kórumbos).

923.t: From Proto-Hellenic *məntʰánō, *mantʰánō, from Proto-Indo-European *mn̥-n-dʰ-, nasal infix present of *men(s)dʰh₁-, itself possibly a *dʰ-extension of *men- (“to think, mind”), thus "to put one's mind".

959.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₃órbʰos (“orphan”), from *h₃erbʰ- (“to change ownership”). Cognate with Latin orbus (“orphaned”), Sanskrit अर्भ (árbha, “small”), Old Armenian որբ (orb, “orphan”).

945.t: From ἶσος (îsos), itself from earlier *ϝῖσϝος (*wîswos), of disputed origin: * The Cretan and Arcadocypriot forms suggest Proto-Hellenic *wíswos, perhaps from a Proto-Indo-European *wi- (“to separate”).

912.t: Possibly from Proto-Hellenic *plát͏̌t͏̌ō, from earlier *plátʰyō, of uncertain origin.

951.t: From Proto-Indo-European *tḱey- (“to settle”). Cognates include Sanskrit क्षेति॑ (kṣéti), Avestan 𐬱𐬀𐬉𐬌𐬙𐬌 (šaēⁱti) and, via Iranian borrowing, Old Armenian շէն (šēn).

914.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʰímər, R-stem derivation from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰeym- (“winter, snow”), complementing the n-stem reflex found in χειμών (kheimṓn). Perhaps originally meaning "winter/year-old (goat)".

964.t: From Proto-Hellenic *dóru, from Proto-Indo-European *dóru. Cognates include Sanskrit दारु॑ (dā́ru), Old Persian 𐎭𐎠𐎽𐎢𐎺 (d-a-ru-u-v /⁠dāruv⁠/) and Old English trēow (English tree).

967.t: From Proto-Indo-European *pléth₂os (“breadth”). Cognates include Sanskrit प्रथस् (práthas), Avestan 𐬟𐬭𐬀𐬚𐬀𐬵 (fraθah), Old Armenian լայն (layn), Welsh lled.

993.t: From Proto-Indo-European *keyh₂- (“to start to move”). Compare κίω (kĭ́ō, “to go”) and κίνυμαι (kī́nŭmai, “to go; move”), Latin cieō (“to move”).

913.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dʰrogʰós (possibly an -ός (-ós) nominal), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰregʰ- (“to run, drag, pull”), whence τρέχω (trékhō, “to run”).

915.t: From Proto-Hellenic *(w)ə́rsēn, from Proto-Indo-European *wérsēn (“male”); however, dialectal attestations show it had no initial digamma in Greek, and it has been argued that the initial w was lost in the Greek, Armenian, and some Indo-Iranian forms of…

970.t: From Proto-Hellenic *statʰmós, from Proto-Indo-European *sth₂-dʰ-mó-s, from *steh₂- (“to stand”).

948.t: Shortened form of βοηθόος (boēthóos, “hasting to the cry for help”), from βοή (boḗ, “shout, call”) + θοός (thoós, “swift”, from θέω (théō, “run”)).

947.t: Traditionally taken as an o-grade nominal formation from Proto-Indo-European *serḱ- (“to mend, fence”), whence also ἕρκος (hérkos, “fence”), i.e. "the bounds that one assumes" > "obligation, oath".

938.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *pleh₁- Proto-Indo-European *-yōs Proto-Indo-European *pléh₁yōs Proto-Hellenic *pleíhōn Ancient Greek πλείων From Proto-Hellenic *pleíhōn, from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₁is-ō.

966.t: From μή (mḗ, “not”) + ποτέ (poté, “ever, at some time”).

935.t: From κοπία (kopĭ́ā, “rest from toil”) + -άω (-ắō), from κόπος (kópos, “beating, suffering, work”) from κόπτω (kóptō, “to strike”).

901.t: Unknown; probably Pre-Greek. More at ψάω (psā́ō).

927.t: From Proto-Indo-European *gʰreh₂w- (“to rush in, attack”). Cognate with Latin ingruō (“to attack”), Lithuanian griáuti (“to destroy”), griū́ti (“to crumble”).

974.t: From Biblical Hebrew מִיכָיָה (Mîḵāyāh, “Who is like Yah?”).

998.t: Borrowed from Biblical Hebrew שִׁמְעִי (Šimʿī, “Shimei”, literally “renowned”).

973.t: From Proto-Hellenic *oneidos, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃neyd-os (“blame, revilement”); compare Gothic 𐌽𐌴𐌹𐌸 (neiþ), Sanskrit निन्दा (nindā́), Latvian naids.

905.t: From ἐπιτηδεύω (epitēdeúō, “to pursue an activity, to practise a thing”) + -μα (-ma).

922.t: Altered from earlier κρέσσων (kréssōn), from Proto-Indo-European *kretyōs, from *kret- (whence κρατύς (kratús)). Synchronically, κρατύς (kratús) + *-ϳων (*-jōn).

968.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pluňňō, from a nasal-present formation of Proto-Indo-European *plew- (“to wash”), the same root of Latin pluit (“it rains”) and Old Armenian լուանամ (luanam, “to wash”).

957.t: According to Beekes, possibly from a disyllabic Proto-Indo-European root *h₂erh₁- (“to please, satisfy”), which appears to be related to *h₂reh₁- (“to think, reason, arrange”), apparently reanalyzed from *h₂réh₁(ye)ti, a stative-durative verbal form from…

920.t: Traditionally derived from a Proto-Indo-European *delH- (“to reckon”) (which De Vaan considers to be possibly the same root as *delh₁- (“to split”)), and compared with Latin dolus (“fraud, malice”), Oscan dolom (“intention, ruse”), Proto-Germanic *talō…

955.t: From the root of ποιμήν (poimḗn, “shepherd”) + -αίνω (-aínō), from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂- (“to protect, shepherd”). Compare Latin pāscō (“to tend, feed, nourish”), Late Latin pāscor (“to feed onself, eat; pasture, graze”).

949.t: From γλύφω (glŭ́phō, “to carve, engrave”) + -τός (-tós, adjectival suffix).

902.t: From ἀνα- (ana-, “up”) + τέλλω (téllō, “to perform, accomplish, rise”).

940.t: From the same Pre-Greek source as σπέος (spéos) and σπῆλυγξ (spêlŭnx).

956.t: From the root of συνίημι (sŭnī́ēmĭ, “perceive, understand”) + -τός (-tós).
